label: D-4 part-time work: Korean proficiency standard
appliesTo: D-4-1 language trainees applying for a part-time work permit
why: The proficiency bar decides how many hours a student may work, so it is a budget input, not a language goal. It sits in administrative guidance and has been revised before.

history.source: Study in Korea — residence and stay information
history.note: Accepted equivalents include completing KIIP stage 2, scoring 41 or above on the KIIP pre-assessment, or beginner level at a King Sejong Institute. Falling short does not bar work outright; it narrows the permitted hours.
